comments.author: coder543
comments.story_title: Measuring Latency in Linux (2014)
comments.why_zh: 常被引用的、解释时间处理为何困难的说明
comments.quote_zh: 一个常被引用的 YouTube 视频讲时间，解释了为什么这件事很难
comments.text_zh: 不管用什么编程语言，这都是个难题。有一个常被引用的 YouTube 视频讲时间，解释了为什么这件事很难：[视频] 一个合理的初步近似方案是：每隔一秒（或一分钟、一小时，视需求而定）检查一次，看当前系统时间是否已经晚于任何待处理事件的计划时间。然后你大概还想确保事件被标记为已完成，这样即使时钟倒拨，它们也不会再次触发。想预测从现在到周六下午 3 点之间该休眠多少秒是件困难的事，但如果足够重要，你大概可以用某个时间库来做……可要是政府突然宣布从现在到那时的时区偏移发生变更呢？预测式方案就会在错误的时间醒来。
comments.text: That’s a hard question regardless of programming language. One commonly referenced YouTube video about time that explains why this is hard: [VIDEO] A reasonable first approximation of a solution would be to just check every second (or minute, or hour, depending on requirements) whether the current system time is later than the scheduled time for any pending events. Then you probably want to make sure events are marked as completed so they don’t fire again if the clock moves backwards. Trying to predict how many seconds to sleep between now and 3pm on Saturday is a difficult task, but you can probably use a time library to do that if it’s important enough... but what happens when the government suddenly declares a sudden change to the time zone offset between now and then? The predictive solution would wake up at the wrong time.

comments.author: jonathansampson
comments.story_title: Goodbye Brave
comments.why_zh: 总结程序员处理时间时面临的问题
comments.quote_zh: 它精彩地总结了程序员处理时间时面临的问题 :)
comments.text_zh: 好问题！日期和时间是编写软件时最令人深恶痛绝的障碍之一，尤其是软件需要在全球不同地区、不同时区的数百万台设备上以特定方式运行。在我们的案例中，有一小段代码旨在计算距离午夜/明天还有多长时间。但当时钟在午夜发生变化（向前或向后跳）时，你可能会遇到长度似乎超过 24 小时的日子。而当一天的长度超过约 24 小时，那些看似简单的数学等式就会给出意想不到的结果。一段负责设置计时器的逻辑，在我们的“距离明天还有多久”代码开始返回负数时，最终安排了一大堆计时器。那组非预期的计时器把应用本身锁死了。你可以在这里看到我们针对该行为提交的 issue：[LINK] 。想体验 10 分钟的焦虑，可以看看 Computerphile 的 Tom Scott 的“The Problem of Time & Timezones”：[VIDEO] 。它精彩地总结了程序员处理时间时面临的问题 :) Sampson（Brave Team）
comments.text: Great question! Dates and times are one of the most loathed obstacles in writing software that needs to work a particular way across millions of devices situated all across the globe in different regions and time zones. In our case, we had a bit of code that aimed to measure the time until midnight/tomorrow. But when clocks change at midnight (jumping forward or backward), you can wind up with days that appear to be longer than 24 hours in length. And when a day is more than ~24hr in length, you wind up with unexpected answers to seemingly simple math equations. A bit of logic, responsible for setting up a timer, wound up scheduling numerous timers when our 'How long until tomorrow' code began returning negative numbers. That set of unintended timers locked-up the application itself. You can see our issue for the behavior here: [LINK] . For 10 minutes of anxiety, check out 'The Problem of Time & Timezones' from Tom Scott of Computerphile: [VIDEO] . It's a fantastic summary of the issues programmers face when dealing with time :) Sampson (Brave Team)

comments.text_zh: 对于以 TLD 形式存在的国家所官方承认的、当前形式的国别时区，那也许行得通；但 tz database 包含更多当前时区，更重要的是还有大量历史时区。仅在 DNS 中表示当前已承认时区的历史形式就会是一团乱，更不用说那些与当前存在并拥有 TLD 的国家无关的时区了。edit：这期视频很棒，解释了很多原因，说明为什么时区远没有你想象的那么直截了当：[VIDEO]
comments.text: That might work for the current form of the country-specific time zones officially acknowledged by countries that exist in TLD form, but the tz database contains many more current time zones more importantly piles of historical time zones. Representing just the historical forms of currently recognized time zones in DNS would be a mess, without even getting in to those that are not associated with a country that currently exists and has a TLD. edit: This is a great video explaining a lot of the reasons why time zones are nowhere close to as straightforward as you may think: [VIDEO]

comments.author: SFJulie
comments.story_title: Maya – Python Datetimes for Humans
comments.why_zh: 作为关于时区问题背景的引用
comments.quote_zh: Computerphile 时区到底有什么问题
comments.text_zh: 它并没有解决：时区（TZ）定义是政治性的、不准确的、愚蠢的，而且没有版本控制。TZ 的问题就出在 TZ 的核心定义本身。1）它们总是在变：如果你已经 3 个月没更新 TZ，那它们很可能已经不准确了 2）你的 TZ 定义也许准确，但在相关时区里可能并没有真正被应用 3）同一经度上可以有不同本地时间 4）同一经度上可以是不同的日期…… 5）TZ 没有版本控制，如果在你生成的两条记录之间 TZ 变了，你存下的时间区间就是不准确的。我们并没有 API 能把 TZ 随时间的变化考虑进去。6）CEST/DST 打破了时间是单调递增函数这条公理 参考 PostgreSQL 手册 8.5.3 TZ [LINK] Computerphile 时区到底哪里有问题 [VIDEO]
comments.text: It does not: timezone (TZ) definitions are politicial, inaccurate, and stupid and non versioned. The problem with TZ is TZ in its core definition. 1) they always change: if you have not updated your TZ since 3 months they are probably inaccurate 2) your TZ definition maybe accurate but they may not have been applied for real in the concerned zone 3) you can have different local time for the same longitude 4) you can have different days on the same longitude ... 5) TZ are not versioned, if the TZ changed between 2 records you may have made, you have inaccurate intervals stored. We do NOT have an API to take TZ change over time in consideration. 6) CEST/DST is breaking the axiom that time is a growing monotonic function References 8.5.3 TZ in postgresql man [LINK] Computerphile what's wrong with timezones [VIDEO]

comments.author: DavidPeiffer
comments.story_title: Timezone Bullshit
comments.why_zh: 结论：使用现成的时间库，从此不用再担心。
comments.quote_zh: 使用他们的开源代码，给他们署名，然后永远别再担心这件事。
comments.text_zh: 我不太确定自己有没有跟上（而且这周时区和时间处理对我的工作真的很重要，所以我真的很想弄明白）！如果用户提供一个时间为 11/7/2021 1:50 AM America/New_York，既然这正是夏令时结束的时候，库如何判断它是 -5 还是 -4 偏移？我相信这就是 GP 所指的歧义。我正在尝试把我在用的几个系统之间的时间对齐。一个提供带偏移的 GMT 时间（干净且有用），另一个系统报告时区和本地时间，还有一个系统完全不知道它什么时候在时区之间切换，但会一致地基于单个时区报告时间。这不是在处理过去多个时区的情况，它让我想起 Tom Scott 关于处理时间和时区的视频，结尾总结大致是：“去找一个已经构建了处理时间库的人，狠狠感谢他们，使用他们的开源代码，给他们署名，然后永远别再担心这件事。” [VIDEO]
comments.text: I'm not sure I follow (and this week, timezones and time handling are really important for my job, so I really want to understand)! If a user provides a time of 11/7/2021 1:50 AM America/New_York, how does the library determine if it's a -5 or -4 offset given that's when daylight savings time ends? I believe that's the ambiguity GP is referring to. I'm trying to align time across a few systems I work with. One provides a GMT time with an offset (clean and useful), another system reports timezones and local time, and yet another system has no idea when it moves between time zones, but reports time based on a single timezone consistently. Not dealing with multiple timezones in the past, it reminds me of Tom Scott's video on handling time and timezones, summarized at the end as roughly "Go find someone who built a library for handling times, thank them profusely, use their open source code, give them credit, and never worry about it again." [VIDEO]
